reader.requirement: At --std 85, when the program collating sequence is an ALPHABET literal phrase in which ALSO puts several characters at one position, FUNCTION CHAR of that position must return the character of the first literal written for it (literal-1, nonnumeric or numeric ordinal), in the program and in every contained program; positions held by one character (single, multi-character, THROUGH literals, unspecified native characters) return that character.

edition-consulted.switches: the D8 window: CHAR IntroducedIn 85 against Edition.DialectLevel
Edition.DialectLevel < 2002 returns early for the IS LOCALE phrase (refused at recognition below 2002); the literal phrase does not reach this arm
refuses the FOR ALPHANUMERIC/NATIONAL phrase below 2002 (COBOL0900); a 1985 literal phrase without FOR is unaffected

reader.edition-search: Grepped SpecialNamesBinder.Alphabets.cs, SpecialNamesBinder.Literals.cs, CollatingModel.cs, ImplementorCodeNames.cs, CollationEmit.cs for DialectLevel, Edition.Edition, IsActive(, Has(: only the LOCALE early return and the RangeInAlphabet2002 gate (a THROUGH-range IN phrase, not on this path). The repByPos (first occupant of a position) construction and the runtime CharAt are edition-free.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f06_09 covers nonnumeric ALSO groups and the top position; not exercised there: a numeric literal-1 in an ALSO group, a numeric ALSO operand, ALSO after a multi-character literal and a THROUGH run, a subscripted or expression argument, and CHAR in a contained program under the containing program's sequence.

reader.notes: AlphabetLiteralPhrase records, per position, the first character assigned to it (repByPos; ALSO operands are assigned in source order with literal-1 first), and LiteralPhraseCollation.CharAt returns that representative; ORD and CHAR are exact inverses. Side observation outside this rule: the COBOL1906 duplicate-character diagnostic at --std 85 cites only §2023:12.3.7.3 SR14 a, not the 1985 rule.

refuter.evidence: Attacked the 1985-only literal forms the reader did not try: §1985 SR5 forbids only symbolic-character figurative constants, so SPACE/QUOTE/ZERO/HIGH-VALUE/LOW-VALUE are legal ALPHABET literals, and GR7 makes HIGH-VALUE/LOW-VALUE there the native highest/lowest characters. rc1 (runs/rc1-001): ALPHABET AL IS SPACE ALSO "B" ALSO "A" QUOTE ALSO "Q" ZERO ALSO "Z" "M" ALSO "N" "k" ALSO LOW-VALUE printed C1=SPACE C2=" C3=0 C4=M C5=k, OA=1 OQ=2 O0=3 (literal-1 each time). rc2/rc5 (runs/rc2-001, rc5-001): HIGH-VALUE ALSO "H" -> CHAR(1) is U+FFFF, which rc4 (runs/rc4-001) shows is the native HIGH-VALUE of this implementation (ORD 65536), so literal-1 per GR7; "x" ALSO LOW-VALUE -> CHAR(2)=x. rc3 (runs/rc3-001): an ALPHABET with ALSO that is NOT the program collating sequence leaves CHAR native (CHAR(66)=A, CHAR(114)=q). cite.py: 'OK  §1989:A.2.9.4 RV1  (2.9.4 Returned Values)  the text is in RV1'; 'OK  §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR7  (4.5.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR7'; 'OK  §1985:VI.4.5.3 SR5  (4.5.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR5'.
